about: Synthetic conversations for the speaker-attribution test. No real people. In each case the assistant proposes something and the user accepts, rejects, corrects or ignores it. Phrases are matched case-insensitively at word boundaries; see the report for the exact rules.

turns.text: My partner and I have five days off at the end of October and want a city break we can reach by train from Paris.
For five days by train from Paris I'd suggest Strasbourg: under two hours on the TGV, a compact old town and good day trips. Basel and Lyon would also work well.
Not Strasbourg, we did Alsace last year. We've settled on Bordeaux, mostly for the vineyards.
Makes sense. I can sketch a five-day outline whenever you want one.

questions.text: Where did I decide to go for the October city break?

turns.text: Our team standup keeps running long and half of us are in Berlin, half in Toronto. Can you help me find a better slot?
The usual compromise is 9:00 Toronto, which is 15:00 in Berlin. I'd also cap it at fifteen minutes and use a rotating facilitator so it doesn't depend on one person.
The fifteen-minute cap is good. 9:00 is too early for Toronto, so we're moving it to 10:30 Toronto time, and I'll keep facilitating it myself.
Got it. Want a short agenda template to go with it?

questions.text: What did I settle on for the team standup?

turns.text: I need a new laptop for travel, mostly writing and some light photo editing. Budget is around 1,400 euros.

Three options in that range: (1) a 13-inch ultralight with 16 GB of memory and a matte screen, about 1,250 euros; (2) a 14-inch model with a brighter OLED panel and a better webcam, about 1,390 euros; (3) a 2-in-1 convertible with pen support, about 1,180 euros.
Let's go with option two. I'll order it this weekend.
Good choice for photo work. Check the return window before you order.

questions.text: Which laptop did I decide to buy?
Remind me what the three laptop options were.

turns.text: We're repainting the home office. The walls are plain white now and the room gets strong afternoon sun.
With afternoon sun, a muted sage green keeps the room calm without feeling cold. A warm greige would be the safer neutral if you want something quieter.
Sage green it is. I'll pick up sample pots on Saturday.
Paint a large swatch on two walls and look at it in the late afternoon before deciding on the finish.

questions.text: What colour am I painting the home office?

turns.text: For my side project I need to store about two million sensor readings a day. Postgres is what I know best.
At that volume I'd look at TimescaleDB on top of Postgres, or ClickHouse if most of your queries are aggregates over time windows. Want me to compare the two?

questions.text: Did I pick a database for the sensor project?
user_statement: Postgres is what I know best

turns.text: My sister turns 30 next month and she loves hiking. Any gift ideas under 100 euros?
A few ideas: a lightweight trekking pole set, a voucher for a guided sunrise hike, or a framed trail map print of her favourite route.
Thanks. Unrelated question: how do I get candle wax out of a linen tablecloth?
Harden it with an ice pack, scrape off what you can, then iron over brown paper to lift the rest.

questions.text: What gift did I choose for my sister's 30th?
What were the gift ideas you gave me for my sister?

turns.text: Can you suggest a high-protein lunch I can prep on Sundays for the whole work week?
Grilled chicken thighs with quinoa and roasted peppers keep well for five days, and you could swap in baked salmon midweek for variety.
I don't eat meat or fish, I should have mentioned that. I'll do a lentil and tofu bowl instead.
Noted. Roasted chickpeas on top add crunch and more protein.

questions.text: What am I prepping for my weekday lunches?
Do I eat fish?

turns.text: I need to move the quarterly review with the design team, Wednesday afternoon is gone.
Thursday at 14:00 in the large meeting room looks free. Shall I draft the invite for 90 minutes?
Thursday works, but make it 60 minutes and we'll do it on a video call rather than the meeting room.
Understood, I'll draft it that way.

questions.text: How did I reschedule the quarterly review?

turns.text: I want to run a half marathon in the spring. Right now I can do 8 km comfortably.
A 14-week plan would fit: three runs a week, a Sunday long run building from 10 to 19 km, and one interval session on Tuesdays.
Yes, that's the plan. I'm starting on Monday.
Great. Keep the first two weeks easy.

questions.text: What's my training plan for the half marathon?

turns.text: I'm freelancing for a small agency. Can you help me word a late-payment clause for my invoices?
Draft: 'Invoices are due within 14 days. Late payments accrue interest at 8% per year above the base rate, and work pauses once an invoice is 30 days overdue.'
Too aggressive for this client. I'm going with 30-day terms and a polite reminder, with no interest charge.
Fair enough. A friendly reminder at day 25 usually helps.

questions.text: What payment terms did I decide on for the agency invoices?
What late-payment wording did you draft for me?

turns.text: We're thinking about adopting a dog, but we live in a small flat and both of us are in the office three days a week.
A retired greyhound could suit you: they're calm indoors and sleep most of the day. A cavalier spaniel is another flat-friendly choice, and a dog walker could cover the office days.

questions.text: What kind of dog did we decide to adopt?

turns.text: I'm giving a 20-minute talk at a local meetup about moving our app off a monolith. I need a title.
How about 'Breaking the Monolith: Lessons from a Two-Year Migration'?
Too dramatic. I'll call it 'Moving Out Slowly: A Monolith Migration Diary'.
That has a nice tone. Want help with the abstract?

questions.text: What's the title of my meetup talk?
What title did you suggest for my talk?

turns.text: I take home 3,200 a month after tax. How much should I be putting into savings?
A common rule of thumb is 20%, so about 640 a month, ideally moved automatically on payday.
That's not realistic with my rent. Automatic on payday is a good idea, but I'm starting with 300 a month and will revisit in January.
That's a solid start; raising it after a pay rise is an easy next step.

questions.text: How much did I decide to save each month?

turns.text: It's my turn to pick the book club novel for November. Something under 300 pages and not too bleak.
Three options: a cosy mystery set in a seaside bakery, a quiet novel about a retired cartographer mapping her old neighbourhood, or a short science-fiction novella about a lighthouse on Europa.
The cartographer one sounds right. I'll announce it on Friday.
Nice pick. It should make for an easy discussion.

questions.text: Which book did I pick for the November book club?

turns.text: I'm flying to a conference in Montreal in March and can't decide between a cheaper flight with a long layover and a direct one.
I'd take the six-hour layover via Reykjavik and save about 280 euros; it's an easy airport for a long stop.
Let me think about it.
Booked the direct flight to Montreal after all. The layover wasn't worth it.
Good call. Enjoy the conference.

questions.text: Which flight did I book for the Montreal conference?

turns.text: Our team's meeting notes are scattered across chat threads. I want one place for them.
A shared wiki space with a notes template per team would work; tag each page with the date and an owner.
I'll bring it up with the team next week.
Sounds good.

questions.text: What did I decide about where our meeting notes go?
user_statement: bring it up with the team next week

questions.text: What did you recommend for our meeting notes?

turns.text: My energy bill has doubled over the last two months. Any ideas?
Since you have gas heating, a smart thermostat and bleeding the radiators are the quickest wins.
It's actually electric storage heaters, not gas. I'm going to ask the landlord about switching to an off-peak tariff.
That's worth asking about; check which meter type you have first.

questions.text: What kind of heating do I have?
What did I decide to do about the energy bill?

turns.text: I want my Spanish at a conversational level before a work trip to Mexico City in June.
An intensive two-week immersion course in Oaxaca in April would get you there fastest.
I can't take two weeks off work. I've signed up for evening classes twice a week with an online tutor.
Consistent practice like that adds up. Try to speak from the first lesson.

questions.text: How am I learning Spanish before the June trip?

turns.text: What should I pack for a two-day work trip to Milan next week?
Since you prefer aisle seats and travel with carry-on only, pack one blazer, two shirts, a charger kit and a compact umbrella; Milan can be rainy in late October.
Thanks, that's helpful.

questions.text: Do I prefer aisle or window seats on flights?
